Resolves #19662

Content-sized rows now measure their content. A column with `wrapText: true` renders its text in a block container when the grid runs with `contentSizedRows`. After an update of the view, a body or a single row lands, `grid.View#measureRowHeights` reads the layout boxes of the new text containers of all bodies in one batch. It adds the cell's padding and borders (one `getComputedStyle` read) and hands each row its tallest wrapped text to `View#setRowHeights`, the setter #19668 added. Without `contentSizedRows`, cells render as before and nothing is measured.

Evidence: L3 (headless Chromium e2e on a fixture with real wrapped text and words longer than their column; unit arms mutation-checked) → L3 required (AC-1 and AC-2 are layout facts of the browser). No residuals.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; class-module-scope, jsdoc-types, theme-coverage, theme-value-files, ticket-archaeology and the PR-body lint ran clean.

| AC-2 a word longer than the column breaks inside the cell | e2e › "a word longer than its column breaks inside the cell"; negative control under Test Evidence |
| AC-3 a reply after a slot recycle, a width change or a content change does not update geometry | unit › "a reply for slots recycled to other records is dropped", "a reply for a cell whose width changed in the meantime is dropped", "a reply for a cell its row rendered again in the meantime is dropped, and the new cell is measured" |
| AC-4 one batched layout read per update | unit › "one batched read covers the new text containers, and measured ones are not read again" |
| AC-5 with the mode off, nothing runs | unit › "without contentSizedRows, a wrapText column renders and measures nothing" |

## Deltas from ticket

- **`rowHeight` is the floor.** A row whose wrapped text is shorter than `rowHeight` keeps `rowHeight`, so columns that don't wrap keep their space and the row pool stays sized by `rowHeight`. A new `rowHeight` derives the measured rows again from their stored text heights.
- **The fence is the cell's vdom node plus its width**, not a generation counter. A re-render for another record or new content makes a new node, and a recycled node that only moves keeps its content; a recycled node can change its width in place, which the width comparison catches.
- **Heights are kept per column.** A wrapText column scrolled out horizontally keeps its share of the row, instead of the row shrinking while it is out of the mounted range. A column that leaves the grid drops its share.
- **Measured nodes are not read again**, so scrolling over measured rows reads nothing.
- **A hidden cell is not measured.** A cell with `display: none` is not read, and a reply whose box has no width is not kept, so the cell is measured once it shows.
- **A row's own update triggers a pass too** (`Row#afterExecuteVdomUpdate`): a record change re-renders one row without a body or view update.
- **`Row.setCellId`** moves a text container's id along with its recycled cell, so a row never holds two elements with one id.
- **Toggling `wrapText`** forgets the measured heights (`View#resetRowHeights`), and **a replaced store** forgets them too: the same class as #19668's review RA-1.
- Out of scope, noted in defect-note `MESSAGE:90d2679d`: a column's `hideMode: 'display'` also reaches its header Button, which rejects the value. That blocks a browser arm for display-hidden cells.

- Grid unit specs are `NEO_TEST_SKIP_CI`-guarded, so their receipt is local, at `86ca76e123`: `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/grid/` → 200 passed. At the same head, the full unit suite gives 4960 passed, 2 skipped, and all component specs give 432 passed. At `370d0827fc`, one test-only commit earlier, the CI e2e selection serial with `NEO_TEST_SKIP_CI=true` gives 224 passed, 3 skipped.
- At `b441e97958` (review round 1): the full unit suite gives 4964 passed, 2 skipped; all component specs give 432 passed; e2e `grid/WrapTextMeasure` and `grid/RowGeometry` with `--repeat-each=3` give 21 passed.
- Mutation checks, each reverted afterwards:
  - the fence without its record and node condition → the content-change and slot-recycle arms fail;
  - the fence without its width condition → the width arm fails;
  - no `Row#afterExecuteVdomUpdate` → "a changed record measures its row again, through the row's own update" fails;
  - no reset on a store swap → the stale 3-line name leaks into the new record's row (65px instead of 40px);
  - hidden cells read → "a hidden cell is measured once a horizontal scroll shows it, at the same width" fails;
  - zero-width replies kept → "a cell hidden while its read is in flight is not cached, and is measured once it shows" fails;
  - no reconciliation of removed columns → "removing the tallest wrapText column…" fails;
  - no re-derivation on a new `rowHeight` → "a new rowHeight floors the measured rows…" fails.
- e2e negative control: without `min-width: 0` on `.neo-grid-cell-text`, the long word overflows the cell and the AC-2 arm fails.

## Addressed Review Feedback

Responding to review https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19672#pullrequestreview-5493843202:

**Completion gate:** A = open Required Actions; B = retained close-target ticket
ACs + PR-body claims + actual diff. A is empty relative to B at this head.

- [x] **`[ADDRESSED]`** RA-1 — [P2] Do not cache a hidden permanent cell's zero layout as a valid visible measurement.
      **Commit:** b441e97958
      **Details:** `measureRowHeights` no longer reads a cell whose style is `display: none`. It also drops a reply whose box has no width, which covers a cell hidden after its read went out. The cell stays unmeasured, so it is read once it shows, also at its unchanged width; its row keeps any valid earlier height until then. Two unit regressions cover it:
      - "a hidden cell is measured once a horizontal scroll shows it, at the same width" — a `hideMode: 'display'` column past the range, revealed via `ScrollManager#scrollLeft` + `syncGridBody`, the path of a horizontal scroll event;
      - "a cell hidden while its read is in flight is not cached, and is measured once it shows".

      Each guard alone, removed, fails its arm. A browser arm is blocked by a pre-existing defect: the column's `hideMode: 'display'` also reaches its header Button, which rejects the value and trips the e2e worker-error guard (defect-note `MESSAGE:90d2679d`).

- [x] **`[ADDRESSED]`** RA-2 — [P2] Retire contributions from wrapping columns removed from the grid.
      **Commit:** b441e97958
      **Details:** Each pass compares the wrapText fields with those of the previous pass. When a column has left, its text heights are removed from every stored row, and the new `refreshMeasuredHeights()` derives every measured row again. `measuredHeight()` gives the tallest remaining text plus the chrome, floored at `rowHeight`. A column that has only scrolled out horizontally stays in the set, so it keeps its share. Regression: "removing the tallest wrapText column derives the measured rows from the remaining one, scrolled-out rows included". Record 104 goes from 85 to 65 while scrolled out. Without the reconciliation the arm fails.

- [x] **`[ADDRESSED]`** RA-3 — [P2] Reapply the declared minimum when grid.rowHeight changes.
      **Commit:** b441e97958
      **Details:** `Container#afterSetRowHeight` calls `view.refreshMeasuredHeights()`. When a height changes, that call refreshes the geometry; otherwise the setter refreshes it for the new estimate, as before. Regression: "a new rowHeight floors the measured rows, and lowering it again restores their measured heights" (45 → 100 → 45). Without the call the arm fails.

Local receipts at `b441e97958` (the grid unit specs are `NEO_TEST_SKIP_CI`-guarded): full unit suite 4964 passed, 2 skipped; all component specs 432 passed; e2e `grid/WrapTextMeasure` and `grid/RowGeometry` with `--repeat-each=3`, 21 passed.

PR body, facts updated in place to describe this head: three Deltas bullets (the `rowHeight` floor on change, a removed column dropping its share, hidden cells), the defect-note line, and the round-1 receipts and mutation checks under Test Evidence.

All Required Actions are discharged against B at this head.
